name: Bún cá Ninh Hòa
summary: A Ninh Hòa fish noodle bowl eaten in Nha Trang in the morning and again in the evening. The broth is fish bone with pineapple and tomato. One account pulls cá thu, cá ngừ, and cá cờ; the caption pulls cá bò and cá ngừ.
origin: Ninh Hòa. The provincial digital guide says visitors look for the bowl in Nha Trang. A street number was not printed.
history: The provincial digital guide reprints a Báo Khánh Hòa story from May 2026. It calls bún cá a Ninh Hòa bowl and a Khánh Hòa specialty eaten in Nha Trang.
A Ministry of Culture reprint of Báo Khánh Hòa also prints the name bún lá cá dầm Ninh Hòa. It does not give a second recipe, so that name stays on this bowl.
texture: Fish is steamed, bones removed, and pulled into pieces the provincial digital guide calls cá dầm. The fish cake is fried or steamed after the flesh is pounded until it holds.
howToEat: The provincial digital guide says the broth is fish bone, simmered for hours, with a little pineapple and tomato.
Add herbs cut thin, rau thơm, bean sprouts, and banana blossom. The provincial digital guide says a squeeze of lime, a little chili fish sauce, and a few slices of chili.
The body text says the pulled fish is cá thu, cá ngừ, and cá cờ. The caption says cá dầm is usually made from cá bò and cá ngừ. The cake is from cá đỏ, cá nhồng, and cá thu ảo.
where: Ninh Hòa for the origin. In Nha Trang a shop and a street were not printed. The provincial digital guide names bún cá inside Chợ Đầm, without a stall number.
seoTitle: Bún cá Ninh Hòa — the Nha Trang fish bowl
seoDescription: The provincial digital guide’s bún cá: two fish lists, a clear broth, and a fish cake. Eaten morning and evening. No Nha Trang street was printed.
